_meta.schema: term: id, term, plain (one-line plain English), real (the precise technical statement), ref (man page / authoritative doc on the box)

terms.plain: The free 'run it right here' host Ansible invents when your inventory never mentions localhost.
terms.real: If no inventory entry matches localhost/127.0.0.1, Ansible synthesizes a host 'localhost' with ansible_connection=local and the control node's Python. Defining localhost in inventory replaces this — with whatever vars you gave it.

terms.plain: Run this one task somewhere else — using that machine's settings, not this one's.
terms.real: delegate_to: <host> executes the task on the named inventory host with that host's connection variables, while facts/vars context stays with the original host. delegate_to: localhost rides on the (implicit or explicit) localhost entry.

terms.plain: Skip the copy-then-run dance: pipe the module code straight into remote Python over SSH.
terms.real: [ssh_connection] pipelining=True sends the module payload to the remote interpreter's stdin instead of SFTPing it to remote_tmp and executing. Faster; requires the automation user to be exempt from sudoers requiretty.

terms.plain: The scratch folder on the target where Ansible unpacks each module before running it.
terms.real: Default ~/.ansible/tmp on the target. Module staging fails when it can't be created/used (perms, full disk, noexec) — the disease behind SCAR-002.

terms.plain: The zip-in-a-Python-script wrapper Ansible builds around each module it ships to a target.
terms.real: Ansible bundles the module plus its imports into a self-extracting Python payload (AnsiballZ), stages or pipes it to the target, and executes it with the target's Python.

terms.plain: The scavenger-hunt order Ansible uses to pick which ansible.cfg wins.
terms.real: $ANSIBLE_CONFIG env var, then ./ansible.cfg (current directory — skipped with a warning if the directory is world-writable), then ~/.ansible.cfg, then /etc/ansible/ansible.cfg. First found wins; they do not merge.
terms.ref: man ansible-config; ansible --version shows the winner

terms.plain: The 22-step ladder deciding which definition of a variable wins.
terms.real: From role defaults (weakest) up through inventory group_vars/host_vars, play vars, task vars, to extra-vars (-e, strongest). When a var 'has the wrong value', two rungs are fighting.

terms.plain: Safe to run twice — the second run changes nothing because the state is already right.
terms.real: Modules compare desired state to actual state and act only on the difference, reporting changed vs ok. command/shell are NOT idempotent unless you add creates:/removes:/when: guards.

terms.plain: Rehearsal mode: report what would change, change nothing.
terms.real: Modules with check_mode support predict changed/ok without acting; --diff adds content diffs. command/shell tasks are skipped unless check_mode: false — a clean rehearsal can still hide real changes.

terms.plain: Ansible's word for 'do this with sudo (or another privilege method)'.
terms.real: become: true escalates via become_method (default sudo) to become_user (default root). Password comes from -K, become_password (vaulted), or NOPASSWD sudoers. Missing password = error or silent hang.

terms.plain: The dossier Ansible auto-collects about each host (OS, IPs, disks) at play start.
terms.real: The setup module populates ansible_* variables per host unless gather_facts: false. Conditions and templates referencing facts fail as 'undefined' when gathering is off.

terms.plain: A task that runs only when something actually changed — 'restart the service, but only if the config moved'.
terms.real: Tasks notify: a handler by name; notified handlers run once at end of play regardless of how many tasks notified them.

terms.plain: A module's full legal name: collection + module, like ansible.builtin.copy.
terms.real: Fully Qualified Collection Name. Short names (copy) resolve through a search path; FQCNs are unambiguous and survive collection changes. Write FQCNs in playbooks that must outlive you.

terms.plain: Bare command over SSH — no Python, no staging, no safety net.
terms.real: Executes the command string directly via the connection plugin. The probe for 'is Python-side execution broken?' and the bootstrap tool for Python-less targets. Not idempotent.

terms.plain: Ansible's built-in envelope for secrets — encrypted files that decrypt at run time.
terms.real: AES256 encryption of files or inline values ($ANSIBLE_VAULT header / !vault tag); password supplied at runtime via prompt or file. Secrets never live plaintext in the repo.

terms.plain: One thing systemd manages — a service, mount, timer, socket — described by a small config file.
terms.real: Unit files live in /usr/lib/systemd/system (vendor) and /etc/systemd/system (admin, wins). Edit via drop-ins (systemctl edit); reload the catalog with daemon-reload.

terms.plain: start = now; enable = every boot. They're independent switches.
terms.real: start affects the running state; enable creates the boot-time symlink per the unit's [Install] section. enable --now does both.

terms.plain: The structured log store systemd keeps — queryable by unit, time, priority, boot.
terms.real: Binary indexed journal read via journalctl; persistent when /var/log/journal exists. Size-capped by SystemMaxUse in journald.conf.

terms.plain: The security name-tag on every file and process; mismatched tags get denied.
terms.real: user:role:type:level labels; policy allows process domains to access object types. ls -Z / ps -Z show them; restorecon resets files to policy; semanage fcontext makes custom labels permanent.
terms.ref: RHEL Using SELinux guide (local PDF); man restorecon

terms.plain: SELinux's 'no' — a logged record of exactly what it blocked and why.
terms.real: Access Vector Cache denial in the audit log: source context, target context, class, permission. Read with ausearch -m AVC; explain with audit2why.

terms.plain: firewalld keeps two rule sets: the one running now, and the one that survives reload.
terms.real: Commands change runtime unless --permanent; --permanent alone doesn't touch runtime. The idiom: --permanent + --reload. firewall-cmd --runtime-to-permanent saves live experiments.

terms.plain: RHEL's 'allowed to sudo' club.
terms.real: sudoers ships with %wheel ALL=(ALL) ALL; membership (usermod -aG wheel) grants sudo. Debian's equivalent club is 'sudo'.

terms.plain: rm removes the name; the disk space stays until the last program holding the file lets go.
terms.real: unlink() removes the directory entry; the inode and blocks free only when the link count AND open-handle count reach zero. Found with lsof +L1; freed by restarting the holder.

terms.plain: TERM asks a program to quit and clean up; KILL yanks the power cord.
terms.real: SIGTERM (15) is catchable — handlers flush and exit. SIGKILL (9) is uncatchable — no cleanup, risk of corrupted state. Services: systemctl stop sends the unit's configured stop sequence.

terms.plain: A small extra file that adjusts a vendor config without editing the vendor's copy.
terms.real: systemd: /etc/systemd/system/<unit>.d/*.conf via systemctl edit. sudoers: /etc/sudoers.d/. sshd: /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/. Survives package updates; removable in one delete.
